hints: Look at the three states involved here, gaseous ions, solid lattice and aqueous ions, and think about how they link in a Hess cycle.

Add the two hydration steps together, $\text{Cs}^{+}(\text{g}) \to \text{Cs}^{+}(\text{aq})$ and $\text{Br}^{-}(\text{g}) \to \text{Br}^{-}(\text{aq})$, to get the direct route from gases to solution.
Set that direct route equal to the indirect route via the solid, then rearrange to isolate q for forming the solid from the gases.
walkthrough:
**Picture the Hess cycle**

Think of this as two different ways to go from gaseous ions to aqueous ions. You can go directly by hydration, or indirectly via the solid.

$$\text{Cs}^{+}(\text{g}) + \text{Br}^{-}(\text{g}) \to \text{CsBr(s)} \to \text{Cs}^{+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Br}^{-}(\text{aq})$$

**Calculate the direct route**

Hydration is gaseous ion to aqueous ion, so just add the two given values.

$$\Delta H_{\text{direct}} = \Delta H^{\ominus}_{\text{hyd}}[\text{Cs}^{+}(\text{g})] + \Delta H^{\ominus}_{\text{hyd}}[\text{Br}^{-}(\text{g})]$$
$$\Delta H_{\text{direct}} = (-276) + (-335) = -611 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Write the Hess expression for the indirect route**

The indirect route is first form the solid (this is q), then dissolve the solid.

$$\Delta H_{\text{indirect}} = q + \Delta H^{\ominus}_{\text{sol}}[\text{CsBr(s)}]$$
$$\Delta H_{\text{indirect}} = q + (+25.9)$$

**Solve for q**

By Hess's Law the two routes must be equal, so equate and rearrange.

$$q + 25.9 = -611$$
$$q = -611 - 25.9 = -636.9 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
This large negative value makes sense, as forming an ionic lattice from gaseous ions is strongly exothermic.

options.A: Correct. Hess's Law gives q + 25.9 = -276 + (-335), so q = -611 - 25.9 = -636.9 kJ mol-1. This is the lattice formation enthalpy, strongly exothermic.
options.B: Incorrect. This is -276 - 335 + 25.9 = -585.1. It adds the solution enthalpy instead of subtracting it, which reverses the direction of the dissolving step in the cycle.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the exact opposite sign to B. It corresponds to breaking the lattice apart into gaseous ions (lattice dissociation), not forming it, and also uses the wrong sign for solution.
options.D: Incorrect. This is +636.9, the exact reverse of the correct value. It describes $\text{CsBr(s)} \to \text{Cs}^{+}(\text{g}) + \text{Br}^{-}(\text{g})$, the endothermic separation of the solid into gaseous ions.
